Check whether ASD is sensitive enough to detect protocol differences.
out.other_title: Limitations: simplified training, only two domains, untested protocol variants
out.rationale: Hammond and Adam-Day list not evaluating simultaneous versus sequential debate as a limitation. Sudhir et al. report no significant effect on ASD from switching between simultaneous and sequential debate or changing turn count; this is prompted debate with a gpt-4o-mini judge on GSM8K, not trained neural interactive proofs.
out.scope: proposed ADDRESSES: whether simultaneous versus sequential debate matters, for LLM debate on GSM8K

open_obligations: Note that Sudhir et al. measure ASD while Kenton et al. measure judge accuracy.
Check statistical power in Sudhir et al.'s 100-question demonstration.
Check that GSM8K is among Kenton et al.'s tasks (GSM8KQA) before comparing directly.
out.other_title: Debate ablations: turns, best-of-N, judge few-shot and chain-of-thought have little effect
out.rationale: Kenton et al. report that number of turns, best-of-N, few-shot prompting and judge chain-of-thought have little effect on results across 9 tasks. Sudhir et al. report no significant effect on ASD from changing debate turns (2 or 4) or simultaneous versus sequential order on GSM8K with a gpt-4o-mini judge; both use inference-only prompted agents.
out.scope: proposed SUPPORTS: whether the number of debate turns matters for prompted LLM debate with LLM judges
